prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-facing outdoor scene over a sloped rocky ground plane (~0.5–1.5 m below the camera), showing the camera wearer's own forearms, hands, and blue-shoed right leg at the bottom (brightest, ~0.2–0.8 m away) and another person's lower legs and sandal-clad feet in front and to the upper-left (~1.2–1.8 m away, ~0.8–1.2 m from the wearer's feet). Both people have their upper bodies and heads cropped out of view, with the other person's feet angled forward and slightly right relative to the camera wearer, while the ground pebbles and a small round white stone held within arm's reach (~0.2–0.6 m) are directly below. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer crouches or leans down as their right hand reaches toward the ground (~0.6 m in frames 3–4) and lifts the stone close to the lens (~0.25 m on the right in frame 5), while the other person's legs shift toward the top-left edge and fade into darker depth values. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the wearer's raised right arm and leg from the camouflaged rocky terrain, though it is unreliable along the outer fisheye corners (which turn black) and in frame 5 where the other person's feet nearly vanish into the background gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground human limbs against the unlabelled rocky ground, placing the other person's lower legs and feet in the upper-left (~1.2–1.8 m away, angled toward the camera wearer's right) and the camera wearer's own hands, forearms, and right leg at the bottom (~0.2–0.8 m away, within arm's reach). Both individuals' torsos and heads are out of view, so gaze cannot be observed from the masks, though foot orientation shows the wearer facing forward/downward toward the other person's legs (~0.8–1.2 m ahead). Over the 5 frames, the other person's leg mask recedes toward the upper-left frame boundary as the wearer's right arm extends forward toward the ground in frames 3–4 and rises on the right in frame 5, where the small white stone pinched between the fingers is segmented and labelled as a 'sports ball' (~0.25 m away). This map highlights the exact silhouette of the held object and limb boundaries against the cluttered pebbles better than RGB alone, but it is unreliable in splitting the camera wearer's own body parts into multiple separate 'person' instances with inconsistent colours and straight horizontal cutoffs across the right forearm in frames 4–5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only magenta 2D hand skeletons on a black background, capturing the camera wearer's hands in the lower foreground (~0.2–0.6 m away, within immediate arm's reach) while omitting all body skeletons, legs, feet, and the rocky ground layout. In frame 1, only the wearer's hands overlap at the bottom-left (~0.4 m away); in frames 2 and 4, both the left hand (bottom-left, ~0.5 m) and right hand (bottom-centre/right, ~0.5–0.6 m, ~0.2–0.3 m apart) are tracked, whereas in frame 3 only the left hand and in frame 5 only the raised right hand (middle-right, ~0.25 m away) appear. Because no upper bodies, heads, or the other person's legs (~1.2–1.8 m ahead in the upper-left) are detected due to heavy out-of-frame cropping, facing direction and gaze cannot be determined from this map alone. Across the sequence, the tracked skeletons show the right hand moving forward toward the ground and then lifting upward and opening its fingers toward the camera in frame 5; this makes fine finger articulation and pinch posture much clearer than in the RGB strip, but the map is unreliable when the reaching right hand is completely missed in frame 3 and the left hand is missed in frame 5.
